solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Circle of stones Charlie left in Italian city church

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: 'in' places the abbreviation for left inside the name of the city

parts.note: the Italian capital
L is the usual abbreviation for left
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A sightseer finds a ring of stones abandoned inside a church in some Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie comes from the NATO phonetic alphabet; the left-hand abbreviation lands inside the city name, not after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cromlech is a prehistoric megalithic monument, either a dolmen or a ring of standing stones.

clue.text: Firm undertaking to accept Mike's trade-off

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the phonetic letter is taken inside

parts.note: CO is short for company
a promise is a pledge or undertaking
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A company's formal pledge takes on Mike's deal.
explanation.walkthrough: M slots in between CO and PROMISE; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise is a settlement in which each side gives up something, so a trade-off.

clue.text: Your and my time on radio?

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so pronunciation is what counts

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: A broadcaster talks about the slot that belongs to you and me.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUR, with its silent H, sounds exactly like the possessive word.
explanation.definitionFit: Our is the possessive meaning belonging to us, that is to you and me together.

clue.text: Pushes for places to meet, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: campaigns to influence decision-makers
second meaning: entrance halls, where people often meet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that meeting places is a loose description: these halls are only one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to press politicians on an issue, and lobbies are also hotel foyers and entrance halls.

clue.text: Talk about losing heart in adaptation of building

indicators.note: 'in' places the shortened word inside the longer phrase that follows

parts.note: a conversion turns a building to a new use, such as a barn conversion

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle goes, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Discussion of a disheartening building conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' keeps only its outside letters, which then sit inside CONVERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversation is informal spoken exchange between people, which is talk.

clue.text: Wearing rings, left for wine-exporting city

indicators.note: the rings wear the next word like clothing, so they go around it

parts.note: two rings, each shaped like the letter O
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone wearing rings sets off for a city famous for exporting wine.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT sits between the two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto (Porto) in Portugal is the city that gave its name to port wine, shipped from its lodges.

clue.text: Empire damaged by Republican head of government

indicators.note: a damaged thing is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An empire harmed by a Republican leader of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier is the title for a prime minister, the chief of a government.

clue.text: Idealise Catholic connection, thus rising internally

parts.note: Roman as in Roman Catholic

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the reversed word sits within the connection

parts.note: a tie is a link or connection

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: Someone glorifies a Catholic link that seems to grow from within.
explanation.definitionFit: To romanticise is to present something as better or more glamorous than it is, to idealise it.

clue.text: Reluctant to abandon leader: you can swear it

indicators.note: abandoning the leader means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: loath means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: A loyal follower unwilling to desert a leader makes a solemn vow.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise, and one swears an oath.

clue.text: Dying to bury bone in mass of earth

indicators.note: to bury something is to put it down inside something else, here inside the earth

parts.note: a mound is a heap of earth
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: Someone desperate to bury a bone in a heap of soil, like a keen dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dying to' reads as 'eager to', but 'Dying' alone is the definition and 'to' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means at the point of death, or figuratively in terminal decline.

clue.text: Solitary member of island group meeting Italian

parts.note: Herm is one of the Channel Islands
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: A lone resident of a group of islands encounters an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: Herm is a small island in the Channel Islands, between England and France, near Guernsey. 'Solitary' is used as a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary, as a noun, is a recluse who lives alone, which is what a hermit is.

clue.text: Spoilsports quietly start to reveal mistake in new operas

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: 'in' places the preceding pieces inside the rearranged word
a new version is remade, so these letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: a typo is a typing mistake
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Killjoys quietly begin pointing out an error in some newly staged operas.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged opera letters open up after their first letter to take in the reveal initial and the mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Party poopers are people who dampen others' fun, the same idea as spoilsports.

clue.text: Freezing foreign terrain, mostly wild

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the second word is dropped
something wild is out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
terrain with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A traveller describes an icy, untamed landscape abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Freezing, as a noun, is the act of chilling to keep cold, which is what refrigeration means.

clue.text: Tire at workplace, initially receiving naval chief

parts.note: to flag is to grow tired
an office is a place of work

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An admiral receives visitors at his desk and grows weary.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag officer is a senior naval commander, such as an admiral, entitled to fly a flag.

clue.text: Dogged sibling endlessly dipping into a set of books

indicators.note: to dip into is to go inside, so the shortened word goes inside what follows
without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a as in 'ten pounds a day', meaning per
a sister is a sibling
the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A determined sister keeps dipping into a box set of novels.
explanation.walkthrough: The tiny word 'a' is doing real work: it means 'per', as in a price per item.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged and persistent both describe someone who keeps going stubbornly despite difficulty.

clue.text: Tightfisted son's resources

parts.note: mean means stingy
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A miserly son's assets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'son's' possessive, but it only supplies S.
explanation.definitionFit: Means are a person's money and assets, their financial resources.

clue.text: Gloomy, having a fit during function

indicators.note: during means within a span of time, so these words sit within the trigonometric word

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
a turn is a sudden attack of illness, a funny turn
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is down in the dumps after having a seizure at a social function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' reads as a party but is the mathematical sine.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a sullen, gloomy temperament, once thought to come from the influence of Saturn.

clue.text: Baseball player's two garments

parts.note: the first of the two garments: a pair of short trousers
the second of the two garments: a shirt or blouse

explanation.surface: The two items that make up a baseball player's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the player is the two garments put together.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortstop is the baseball fielder stationed between second and third base.

clue.text: Capital outing, on Long Island principally

parts.note: a trip is an outing

indicators.note: principally suggests the leading part of each word, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A day trip to the main city on Long Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' can mean excellent, as in a capital outing, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Controls tropical weather, so it's said

indicators.note: so it's said tells us to go by how a word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: the rains are the tropical wet season

explanation.surface: A claim that someone can command the weather in the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps for steering a horse, so figuratively the controls of anything.

clue.text: Stocktaker's way to occupy governor, perhaps

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to be inside it, so the street abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: a governor is one kind of ruler, hence the 'perhaps'
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An auditor's route to a seat in the governor's mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: A stocktaker here is someone who takes livestock, not who counts inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals cattle or horses, so literally takes the stock from a farm.

clue.text: Day old American head grasps book's superficiality

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold something in the hand, so the preceding letters hold the next piece

parts.note: FRI is the abbreviation for Friday
O is an abbreviation for old
US is short for American
a ness is a headland
VOL is short for volume

explanation.surface: An elderly American boss clutches a book that is utterly shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' is a headland here, as in Scottish place names like Fife Ness. The book sits just after the day, held by the rest of the chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Frivolousness is a lack of seriousness, the quality of being trivial or shallow.

clue.text: Small wound in rabbit's tail

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a cut is a wound

explanation.surface: A little injury to a rabbit's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Clown about in protective cover

parts.note: Coco the Clown was a famous circus clown
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A clown messing around in a safety suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a celebrated performer with the Bertram Mills Circus in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is the silky case a larva spins to shelter in, hence any protective covering.

clue.text: French poet in US city, one visiting literary compatriot

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so these letters go inside the author's name

parts.note: Jules Verne, a fellow French writer
Los Angeles
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A French poet in an American city visits a fellow French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compatriot' refers back to 'French': a writer from the same country as the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Verlaine was a nineteenth-century French Symbolist poet, companion of Rimbaud.

clue.text: Fury when head avoids sack

indicators.note: if the head is avoided, the word is used without its first letter

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: Anger erupts when the boss dodges being dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger or wrath, the same feeling as fury.

clue.text: Passionate little Dickensian girl switching day and time

indicators.note: switching means the two named letters trade places in the name

parts.note: Little Dorrit is the heroine of the Dickens novel of that name
D is the abbreviation for day
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A steamy Dickens heroine who gets her days and times mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: In DORRIT the D at the front and the T at the end swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrid describes something ardently intense, especially a full-on love affair.

clue.text: Greedy European, one admitted by certain conservationists

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: someone admitted by others is let in, so this letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: sure means certain
the Roman numeral for one
the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: A grasping European is let into some environmental group.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. I goes inside SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for hungry or ravenous, and by extension avaricious.
